narrative.overview:
This is a reading room, not a storefront. The system is built so that a person can arrive curious, sit with a piece of writing or a body of work, and leave without being sold anything. Sobriety comes from what is removed — no gradients on words, no floating glass, no borrowed glow — and warmth comes from what is chosen: a deep navy night (or a warm paper day), a single high-contrast serif that carries every display line, and a blue that behaves like ink on a page rather than a button screaming for a click.

The voice of the writing and the voice of the layout are the same voice. Structure is drawn with hairline rules and negative space, not with boxes; the hierarchy is carried by the type ladder and by air, so that the eye always knows what speaks first. Color is rationed hard: the brand blue governs every interaction — link, hover, focus, selection, active state — and the orange appears exactly once per view, on the one action that matters. That rationing is the discipline that keeps the page calm enough to read.

Everything is token-driven: dark and light are the same system with a swapped palette, and the theme change is a color change, never a layout change. Depth is flat by default; surfaces sit on the page and are separated by one-pixel lines and two soft radial washes, never by resting shadows. The whole build is meant to feel authored — an artifact of one person's practice — rather than generated from a template.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, restrained, patient; clarity before cleverness.
One serif for all display, one sans for all body and labels.
Hairline-led structure: 1px rules define sections, not card chrome.
Blue as the interaction voice; orange reserved for the single primary action.
Flat by default; shadow only as a response to state.
Token-only theming: the same layout in night and paper.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The brand blue owns every interactive state; the orange is spent on exactly one primary action per view. If two things on screen are both orange, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Ink, Not Light Rule
rules.body: The accent is treated as ink on a page: it colors text, underlines, rules, and borders. It is not a light source — no accent glows, no colored shadows on components.

rules.name: The Single Serif Rule
rules.body: One serif for all display, one sans for everything else. Hierarchy is built from scale and air, never from adding a third family.

rules.name: The Marginalia Rule
rules.body: The tracked-caps label is a margin note — numbering, a location, a section marker. It never sits as an eyebrow chip above a heading.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow appears only as a response to state — never as resting elevation, never on cards, never on the orange CTA.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is a one-pixel line, not a box. Prefer a rule or a border color shift over adding a fill or a shadow.

dos: Do set every display line in Libre Caslon Display and everything else in Montserrat; build hierarchy with the token scale and whitespace.
Do theme through tokens only — dark and light must be the same layout with a swapped palette (a token-only change).
Do keep one primary (orange) action per view and let the brand blue own all links, hover, focus, selection, and active states.
Do draw structure with 1px hairline rules and negative space; use the 0.4rem / 0.3rem radii for surfaces and the pill for controls.
Do keep body text at or under 66ch and honor WCAG AA (≥4.5:1 body, ≥3:1 large text and controls) in both themes.
Do keep the logo as vector SVG and preserve a calm, single-gesture motion vocabulary (entrance reveals, theme transition) with prefers-reduced-motion honored.
donts: Don't apply gradients to text or add glow/accent-colored shadows to components.
Don't use resting shadows or floating-glass surfaces; shadow is a response to the detached header only.
Don't introduce a third font family, a second accent hue, or an orange used for anything but the one primary action.
Don't place a tracked-caps label as an eyebrow chip above a heading; the label is marginalia.
Don't add parallax, heavy animation libraries, or motion that is required for content to be readable.
Don't rasterize the isotype or replace it with an icon-font glyph.
